clue.text: Decomposed matter around university smells awful

indicators.note: around tells us the word for smells awful is wrapped round the university letter

parts.note: to hum is British slang for to stink

explanation.surface: Rotting stuff near a campus is giving off a terrible stench.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic soil material formed from rotted leaves and plants.

clue.text: Note from a physician demanding wine

indicators.note: from here means the note is taken away from the physician's name

parts.note: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek physician
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A doctor writes a note asking for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: TE taken out of HIPPOCRATES leaves the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras was a medieval spiced and sweetened drink of the grape.

clue.text: Suitable starter for some sports assemblies

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper

indicators.note: starter for means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Advice on an appropriate opening for certain sporting gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Meets are gatherings for athletics, hunting or racing.

clue.text: Incidental criticism comes as a blow

explanation.surface: Passing disparagement lands like a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a passing critical remark, and also a glancing strike delivered sideways.

clue.text: Refuse to provide food for this animal

definitions.text: Refuse to provide food for this animal

parts.words: Refuse to provide food for this animal
parts.note: reads as a verb phrase about denying an animal a meal, but refuse is the noun rubbish, and rubbish is exactly what this creature eats

explanation.surface: An instruction not to feed a particular animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb (decline); read it as the noun for garbage, which serves as dinner for the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger is a creature that lives off carrion and discarded waste.

clue.text: Honest father seen outside new church

indicators.note: seen outside means the father word surrounds the others

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An upright father is spotted outside a recently built church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and truthful, without deceit.

clue.text: Luckily william Tell was not so lacking in purpose!

definitions.text: Luckily william Tell was not so lacking in purpose!

parts.words: Luckily william Tell was not so lacking in purpose!
parts.note: the legendary archer had to shoot an apple off his son's head, so it was lucky his shot had a target and a steady hand rather than being without direction

explanation.surface: A remark about the Swiss hero who shot an apple from his son's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The word read literally means without aim: a good thing Tell was not, given the apple on his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without direction or goal.

clue.text: Source of river, say, that's rising in a mountain

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the whole string is read from the bottom up
source of gives the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Where a river's headwaters are said to climb a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: R + EG + IE gives REGIE, which 'rising' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous peak in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Soldier capturing a Rabelaisian patriot

indicators.note: capturing means the soldier letters hold the others inside

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Rabelaisian means coarsely humorous, as ribald does

explanation.surface: A soldier captures a bawdy nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the Italian nationalist hero of unification.

clue.text: Direction to change course upset magistrate

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read the other way

parts.note: veer means swerve or change direction
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Instruction to swerve angers a local official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or chief officer in medieval England.

clue.text: Lewis Carroll, possibly, or Falstaff's bogus corporal?

parts.note: pseudo means sham or false
Corporal Nym is one of Falstaff's hangers-on in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor and Henry V

explanation.surface: A literary quiz asking about the author of Alice and a fake soldier from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff's tells you which corporal: Nym, one of his rogues in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Dodgson, an example of an assumed writing name.

clue.text: Horse carrying gold to eastern ravine

indicators.note: carrying means the horse letters hold the gold letters inside them

parts.note: GG, short for gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A pack horse laden with gold heads east towards a canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley, a synonym for a deep cleft in rock.

clue.text: Refuge for person leaving Oman in the existing circumstances

indicators.note: leaving means the word for a person departs from Oman, leaving only its remainder

parts.note: man means a person
as is means in the present state, unchanged

explanation.surface: A man seeks sanctuary after quitting the Gulf state of Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes MAN out of OMAN, leaving O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis, literally a fertile spot in a desert, is figuratively a haven or place of relief.

clue.text: Repulsive river creature — extremely loathsome

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a crab is a creature

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of loathsome

explanation.surface: A revolting crustacean found in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly detestable, synonymous with revolting.

clue.text: A grovelling person, the monitor

explanation.surface: Describing a sycophantic hall monitor at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A reptile is figuratively a mean, fawning person; a monitor lizard is one kind of scaly cold-blooded animal.

clue.text: Material for fitting

explanation.surface: A note about cloth used in dressmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean relevant: material evidence and fitting remarks bear on the matter.

clue.text: Game played by 23 on board

indicators.note: on, with board, means aboard ship, so the referenced word goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: here the board is a ship's, the steamship being SS
the answer to 23 across is a fireplace word, ingle

explanation.surface: A game played on a board by a number of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' conventionally means inside SS (steamship); put the answer to 23 across, INGLE, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Singles is a form of tennis or badminton played one against one.

clue.text: Like the first polished implements one clumsily fired here in Rome

indicators.note: clumsily means the word one is jumbled

parts.note: lit means set alight
hic is Latin for here

explanation.surface: Stone tools from prehistory fired awkwardly in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic, or New Stone Age, was when ground and polished stone tools appeared.

clue.text: One enters freely, being a poet

indicators.note: freely means the letters are released to move about

explanation.surface: Someone walks in without restraint, being a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer is a writer of fourteen-line sonnets.

clue.text: Such excess is singular? Could be, if true

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Pondering whether being excessive is unique, if the claim is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges S with IF TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an overabundance, too much of something.

clue.text: The alternative openings for bright Orpheus and his lute

parts.note: taken as written
or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: openings means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Orpheus and his lyre, with alternative beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorbo is a large bass member of the lute family.

clue.text: Idealistic chap with an aristocratic crest

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage in British English
the crest of a hill is its top
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man with a noble family emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes visionary schemes for a perfect society.

clue.text: Arriviste put out about award for merit

indicators.note: about here means the jumbled letters go around the award
out signals that the word put is rearranged

parts.note: a gold star is a school award for good work

explanation.surface: A newcomer upset about not getting a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns PUT into UPT, which goes 'about' STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a social climber who has risen suddenly to wealth or rank.

clue.text: As a minister she is a busybody, along with Miss Durbeyfield

parts.note: pries means meddles nosily
Tess Durbeyfield is the heroine of Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A female cleric described as nosy, alongside a Hardy heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who performs sacred religious rites.

clue.text: Song from a woman in Eden once

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the old title

parts.note: Anthony Eden was once the British Prime Minister, PM
Sal is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A hymn sung by Eve in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' looks like the Garden, but it is Anthony Eden, UK Prime Minister (PM) 1955-57.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially from the biblical book.

clue.text: He chased the nymphs one day a year

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, one day of the week
yr is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A pursuer of woodland spirits only once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these goat-like woodland gods were notorious for pursuing nymphs.

clue.text: This fireplace is no good in a French island

indicators.note: in means the no-good letters go inside the island word

parts.note: ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A hearth judged useless on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a hearth or chimney corner, an old word for a domestic fire place.

clue.text: Glutton disposing of island's fruit

indicators.note: disposing of means removing the island from the glutton word

parts.note: a gourmand is a greedy eater
Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A greedy eater gets rid of an island's produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is the hard-shelled fruit of plants like squash.

clue.text: About half the Tyne is covered by a social worker

indicators.note: is covered by means the half-word is enclosed within the worker

parts.note: the ant is a social insect, and the worker ant is its labouring caste

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the river's name

explanation.surface: Half the River Tyne in northern England sits under a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes NE from TYNE; a 'social worker' is an ant, not a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anent is an archaic preposition meaning concerning or regarding.

clue.text: Cycled, say, to the game, eating here on the way …

indicators.note: say signals that the word for cycled is heard, not spelt

parts.note: rode means travelled on a bicycle
house, or housey-housey, is the British name for bingo

explanation.surface: Someone rode a bike to a match and ate along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE (housey-housey) is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or restaurant beside a main road serving travellers.

clue.text: There's a vessel at the bottom — or a wreck

indicators.note: a wreck is something smashed up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ship lies on the seabed, possibly a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorboat is a small craft driven by an engine.

clue.text: Wood about right for a little boy to hide in

indicators.note: to hide in means the little boy goes inside the other letters

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A forest fit for a small child to play hide-and-seek in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant timber from a coniferous tree.
